lines.text: The ice cream truck in my grandmother's little town played one song... and came with one rule.
It rolled down Maple Street every summer afternoon, at four o'clock sharp.
But if you ever hear its song after dark... turn off your lights. And never, ever wave.
I spent one summer with her, the year my parents split up.
Every night, the street was silent. Just crickets, moths, and Grandma's porch light buzzing.
Then, in the last week of August, I woke up after midnight... to music.
That same tired song. Slow. Out of tune. Getting closer.
I crept to the window. The truck was parked right outside, glowing pink in the dark.
I kept my hands flat on the sill. I didn't breathe.
Then the little service window slid open... and a small, pale hand reached out, and waved at me.
I didn't wave back. I swear I didn't.
But in the glass, I could see my reflection... smiling. And waving.
